bar.note: iA publishes no latency numbers (only 'boots in a whizz… snappy as jazz'). Bar = best native editors: Sublime 32.5 ms / TextEdit 33.4 ms keyboard-to-photon (Tristan Hume, macOS); internal input→paint ≤5 ms (Typometer, Notepad++ 4.3 ms). Sources in ref/ia/REFERENCE.md.

pieces.title: The page
pieces.judge: the page itself: paper colour, margins, the measure (line length), vertical placement of text in the window, scrolling feel implied by spacing, how the empty space frames the text; overall calm

pieces.title: The type
pieces.what: Duo / Quattro / Mono, size, line height, rhythm
pieces.judge: the typography only: typeface rendering, size, line height, rhythm, weight and colour of the ink, the spacing of blank lines, how italic/bold sit; would a writer rather read and type in this type. Text size and line pitch are set by a published fourteen-step ladder, one pitch per step (docs/design.md, rows Text sizes and Line pitch), so the gap to name is a pitch or a size that misses its own step, not a pitch you would have set differently. Where a state is a crop of the text column rather than a whole window, judge the type inside the crop

pieces.title: Cursor & caret
pieces.judge: the caret and selection only: caret colour, width, height relative to the line, how it sits against the glyphs, blink/motion implied, selection colour; does the caret feel like a precise, alive instrument

pieces.title: Focus & typewriter
pieces.judge: focus mode and typewriter scrolling: how the non-focused text is dimmed (colour, amount), sentence vs paragraph scope, where the active line rests in the window, whether the eye is drawn to exactly the right place

pieces.title: Dark & light
pieces.judge: the two palettes: paper and ink colours, contrast, how dimmed and marker greys read, how the chrome sits on each ground once both sides have bars to sit, whether dark mode feels designed rather than inverted. Until then the comparison is the page, not the furniture around it: one of the two carries bars above and below the text and the other has none, and that is a Piece of its own that has not been built rather than a decision about either ground, so judge the paper, the ink on it and the greys between them and let the bars be

pieces.title: Markup rendering
pieces.what: Headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code, links in the editor
pieces.judge: how Markdown is shown while writing: heading markers, emphasis, lists, blockquotes, code, links — are markers quiet, does the text stay readable, do headings and structure read at a glance without the text jumping

pieces.title: Chrome & menus
pieces.what: Bars, counters, palette, what hides while typing, the empty state
pieces.judge: the chrome: what UI is visible around the text, the stats/word-count bar, title, menus/palette, how it recedes while writing; is there exactly as much interface as a writer needs and no more

pieces.title: File handling
pieces.judge: file handling UI: the library/sidebar, file list, how documents are named and found, open/save affordances, how it looks next to the editor; would a writer trust it with their manuscripts

log.msg: Harness up: headless Chromium screenshots, latency bench, blind A/B pairing. Core editor engine written (textarea + mirror, incremental line render, custom caret, focus/typewriter, markdown tokenizer).

Reference package in: 49 real iA Writer screenshots (App Store, MS Store, ia.net) with verbatim transcriptions, Duo/Quattro/Mono fonts (OFL) with parsed metrics, measured spec sheet (paper #f9f9f9 / #1a1a1a, ink #1c1c1c / #cccccc, caret #00b5ff ≈0.15 em wide, line pitch ≈1.7×, 64-char measure, hanging # markers), latency bar from third-party measurements.

All nine pieces picked blind. Latency won on round 4: app-internal 2.43 ms mean / 15.61 ms worst (bar ≤5/≤16), real keys via /dev/uinput → presented frame 12.17 ms, caret settles 8.1 ms after the key (was 57 ms), cold launch to first document frame 370 ms. Final integration smoke passed in all three fonts and both themes.
